主要内容: Jim Cramer, host of 'Mad Money,' warned investors about the risks of owning retail real estate investment trusts (REITs) due to the decline of brick-and-mortar retail. He highlighted that while retail REITs performed well on a day when the stock market was down, this rally should not be mistaken for a sustainable recovery. Cramer pointed out that rising interest rates could threaten REITs, as they are often seen as bond market equivalents. He emphasized that long-term interest rates must rise due to a booming economy and the Federal Reserve's tightening cycle, which could further hurt REITs, especially those focused on malls. Cramer also noted that the retail industry is facing challenges from the rise of online shopping, with Credit Suisse predicting that 20-25% of U.S. malls could close within five years. Despite this, the number of malls in the U.S. has not decreased, partly due to incentives offered by municipalities. Cramer concluded that the retail REIT sector is over-stored and not a good business to be in, even though rising yields might make these stocks more attractive in the future. Cramer also warned that retail REIT stocks remain very risky to own. He emphasized that while these stocks have shown recent strength, investors should not be fooled. Cramer pointed out that if retail REITs are unable to fill vacancies or are forced to lower rents, dividend cuts could occur. He highlighted the importance of diversification, noting that companies like Federal Realty have already moved away from retail. As property values decline, other escape plans, such as going private, become less viable. Cramer concluded that as interest rates rise again, these stocks are likely to decline. He advised investors to consider reducing their exposure to these REITs, especially those with high yields, as they may signal underlying dividend risks.
